Within the next few years, most of mathematics will be able to be formalized in such a way that mathematicians can explore, build on, and make use of formal libraries. tech.title: Decoherence
tech.summary: Decoherence is the accumulation of locally valid but mutually incompatible or redundant models within a system. It causes the cost of change to be dominated by translating among those models and preventing unintended side-effects. Decoherence grows relative to the rate of change of a system, and it increases faster the more decoherent a system is, resulting in runaway exponential growth. It rules out the specter of runaway recursive self-improvement, as decoherence both prevents AI from improving in a bubble and limits the rate at which it can improve outside of it. However, it also introduces a new kind of disaster called Decoherence Collapse.

tech.title: Will it be a golden age or a dark age for mathematics (and science)?

However, it could also lead to independent human scientific activity progressively weakening, the production of new knowledge becoming increasingly concentrated in a small number of hands, and knowledge becoming alien to human understanding. The future will likely be a combination of these scenarios.

infosec.title: Frozen Privilege: Remote Code Execution in Snowflake-Managed PostgreSQL
infosec.summary: Varonis researchers found that Snowflake-managed PostgreSQL's non-superuser snowflake_admin role could be escalated to OS-level RCE by chaining five documented PostgreSQL features, defeating every published mitigation without disabling any. The chain used CREATEROLE to self-grant pg_write_all_data and hijacked a pg_cron job to run as postgres. It then rebound blocked functions through LANGUAGE internal, exposing tenant mTLS keys and AWS STS credentials and allowing an overwrite of archive_command. Snowflake has fixed the issue server-side, but teams running their own PostgreSQL should treat CREATEROLE as near-superuser, block LANGUAGE internal and C function creation, and audit pg_cron jobs and SECURITY DEFINER functions.

infosec.title: Fake Claude, ChatGPT Attacks Surge, Putting Developers at Risk

ClickFix-style commands appeared in 45% of cases. Targets risk losing source code, SSH keys, CI/CD tokens, cloud and AI API keys, sessions, and billing access.

infosec.title: Exposing AdFection: How Discover-Tech Turned Targeted Ads Into a Pipeline for Zero-Click Mercenary Spyware
infosec.summary: Citizen Lab links Israeli ad company Discover-Tech to zero-click delivery of Candiru spyware through targeted advertisements. Its Controlium platform lets customers select targets by mobile ad ID, cookie ID, or IP address, then run JavaScript when an ad is rendered. At least 45 Al Jazeera devices were infected in 2024 and 2025. Nearly four billion bidding records show ads across almost 200,000 sites and apps. Google, IAB Europe, Beeswax, Vungle, and Eskimi cut Discover-Tech's access after disclosure. A separate actor, DARK CARTOGRAPHER, used the infrastructure to link advertising IDs with phone numbers.

infosec.title: Big Fish: Exploiting a 37-Year-Old Kernel Bug in OpenBSD
infosec.summary: Calif reported two OpenBSD vulnerabilities that enabled local privilege escalation to root. A signed 16-bit shared-memory attachment counter, dating to the original BSD sources, could overflow after repeated forking and wrap to a negative value. That enabled a use-after-free race condition. A separate out-of-bounds write gave the exploit a write-what-where primitive. The exploit worked with KARL, SMAP, and SMEP enabled, using heap grooming, SysV shared-memory manipulation, IP multicast socket allocations, and PTE self-referential mapping changes to reach kernel execution.

infosec.title: Heartbreaker: Metamorphic ransomware comes for macOS
infosec.summary: Heartbreaker, a previously undetected Rust ransomware for Apple Silicon Macs, encrypts files in ~/Downloads with AES-256-GCM, persists through a LaunchAgent, and then rebuilds itself by mutating its own embedded source code and recompiling with Cargo to change its hash each run. Patrick Wardle found the rebuild fragile and noisy because it may install Rust on the fly, depends on a now-deleted GitHub framework, and uses a single hard-coded key that lets victims decrypt every file for free. His open-source RansomWhere? tool still caught it by flagging an untrusted process that rapidly writes high-entropy files, which shows why behavior-based detection holds up against mutating binaries better than hash-based signatures.

infosec.title: CVE Intel

It runs as a Tauri desktop app, CLI, REST API, or MCP server, and its built-in llama.cpp model explains findings locally by default. Teams can also integrate it into CI to fail builds on vulnerable dependencies or rank scanner output using real exploitation signals rather than CVSS alone.

It maps 33 regimes, including the EU roadmap, OMB M-26-15, DORA, and PCI DSS v4.0.1, to buffered priority and full-migration dates, then prices compression, refresh-funded savings, and the cost of delaying migration by one to three years. Each unit cost is labeled by source and editable, allowing CISOs and finance partners to stress-test the numbers before discovery replaces the estimates.

devops.summary: CLI-Anything is a tool that converts software with a codebase into command-line interfaces for AI agents. The project currently supports 18 applications, including GIMP, Blender, and LibreOffice, with 2,461 passing tests. Users can install the CLI-Hub package manager to browse and deploy these community-built CLIs.

devops.title: Deploy with Void
devops.summary: VoidZero has open-sourced Void, a toolchain that extends Vite to handle full-stack application development and deployment. The package includes an SDK, a CLI, and a Platform for teams to self-host deployment environments within their own Cloudflare accounts. It automatically provisions resources like databases and queues during deployment.

devops.title: Azure Maia 300 Architecture Deep Dive
devops.summary: Microsoft's third-generation AI accelerator uses TSMC N2P with 288 GB HBM4 at 18 TB/s. Racks hold 96 accelerators at 167 kW, scaling to 12,288-chip superpods, with up to 7x token throughput.

devops.title: Atlantis at Scale
devops.summary: Details running Atlantis v0.47.1 as a single-replica StatefulSet with Redis locking and S3 plan storage. Limits include an alpha drift API with no scheduler and no cross-project dependency graph. Spacelift positions itself as the alternative.

devops.title: Signals & Levers: Systems Thinking Tools to Unblock Software Delivery
devops.summary: Metrics look green, but releases keep slipping. Elisabeth Hendrickson and Joel Tosi show how to separate signal from noise, map why fixes backfire, and find levers that actually unblock delivery. Get the book

devops.title: Amazon ECS Adds LiveTaskCount Service Metric
devops.summary: A free metric counts tasks that are activating, running, or deactivating, without Container Insights.

devops.title: Powering European Scientific Discovery with Advanced AI Compute
devops.summary: Google DeepMind and Google Cloud will give up to 200 European researchers access to AlphaFold 3, WeatherNext, and other models, plus USD 3 million in compute credits.

data.title: Run Python, Rust, Go, or C++ directly on your ClickHouse data
data.summary: Bring your favorite libraries and custom logic straight into SQL. Upload your code and dependencies;ClickHouse Cloud runs it alongside your live data, with no separate execution service to deploy. Executable user-defined functions are now generally available. Classify customer feedback with Jev or Hugging Face Transformers, catch anomalies with PyTorch, or uncoverpatterns in sensor data with SciPy. Spot problems as data arrives. Try it with $300 in free ClickHouse Cloud credits.

data.title: Under the hood, off the hot path: How D1 scales to millions of databases
data.summary: Cloudflare's D1 serverless SQLite platform keeps query traffic at the edge while its control plane manages millions of tenant databases. Lifecycle operations use idempotent, recoverable flows, with Postgres for transactional metadata, edge KV for routing, and queues for eventually consistent work. The transferable design is to isolate central coordination from the data path so provisioning failures can be repaired without slowing queries.

data.title: A Graph Has No Centre
data.summary: Graph tools for MCP should return focused, bounded views instead of dumping broad subgraphs and hoping prompts impose structure later. The key design move is to make scope explicit in the server through named views, validation rules, and controlled navigation points. For changing entities like avatars, modeling location over time preserves auditability and keeps behavior consistent across clients.

data.title: The Self-Organizing Data Stack
data.summary: Autonomous data platforms need stable logical assets, not fragile table-and-DAG definitions. This proposed architecture keeps consumer contracts and semantic definitions persistent while a runtime synthesizes, consolidates, verifies, and atomically rewires physical pipelines as needs change. Its strongest safeguard is independent verification against business invariants, plus escalation whenever meaning is ambiguous. Language models may draft changes, but cannot authorize them.

data.title: Which LLM should run your agentic analytics? Accuracy vs. cost of Claude, Gemini and GPT
data.summary: Opus delivered the best analytics reports but cost more. Routing by task balances quality and cost: Sonnet for metrics and trends, Gemini Flash for guided analysis with human review, and Opus for root cause investigations.

data.title: Data Engineering Is the Cache Invalidation Problem Ft. Josh Wills
data.summary: Large Spark and Ray jobs offer the wrong feedback loop for autonomous coding: errors and cost often appear only after hours of distributed execution. Data engineers remain responsible for the materialization choices and failure cases agents cannot evaluate cheaply. The practical response is not blind generation, but representative tests, cost-aware guardrails, and human review where pipelines lack fast feedback.

data.title: Apple, AWS, Coinbase and Intuit engineers on what actually worked in production
data.summary: One free virtual day, Nov 4, to skip months of trial and error. NEXT QUERY 2026: 20+ sessions on the analytics systems behind people, apps and agents, where teams running them share architecture decisions, tradeoffs and fixes, with live Q&A. By PhoenixAI (the original creator of StarRocks). Register free · Agenda

data.title: prompt_jev() now works on images
data.summary: MotherDuck's prompt_jev() now analyses images directly in SQL, returning structured answers and confidence scores that can be queried alongside other data. In MotherDuck's food-image benchmark, it processed 1,010 photos for about $0.06 at 90.2% accuracy, rising to 97.7% when keeping only the 81% of results with high confidence.

data.title: Differential storage for DuckDB
data.summary: duckdb-differential brings version-control-style workflows to DuckDB, adding snapshots, time travel, branches, clones, and restore through SQL. The core idea is to preserve known-good database states so teams can test imports, run experiments, and reproduce reports without copying entire databases. Shared immutable chunks keep versions efficient, while optional S3 publishing extends those states for remote access and recovery.

data.title: Introducing Timestral
data.summary: Mistral's Timestral models forecast multiple related time series, estimate uncertainty, and incorporate known future inputs such as production schedules. They run on CPUs without task-specific training, and Mistral reports that its largest model, with 209 million parameters, outperforms larger rivals across three public forecasting benchmarks.

data.title: Tempo 3.1 Release: Kafka, Trace Redaction, and TraceQL Metrics
data.summary: Grafana Tempo 3.1 makes Kafka-backed tracing easier to run with TLS, additional authentication methods, rack-aware reads, and configurable producer compression. Query-based redaction can permanently remove sensitive trace data without enumerating trace IDs, while sampling-aware TraceQL metrics improve analysis of incomplete telemetry. Operators should use redaction dry-runs and complete the upgrade before applying time-bounded deletions.

data.title: AI in Production: Panellists Highlight Silent Failures, Harness Engineering, and Agent Governance
data.summary: Agentic systems can fail while conventional telemetry stays green: semantic drift can corrupt business meaning, and an embedding-model update can abruptly change policy decisions. Production controls therefore need continuous evals fed by live edge cases, separate agent identities with tiered permissions, and human approval of business risk. Treating agents as ordinary application code or relying on prompts for security leaves blind spots.

data.title: Reliable GPU compute for large training & inference jobs
data.summary: Large GPU jobs fail for many small infrastructure reasons, so reliability has to be continuous rather than reactive. Netflix built a layered system that validates nodes before jobs start, monitors hardware during runs, and automatically drains, reboots, resets, or replaces bad machines. The result is more usable GPU capacity and fewer long training or inference runs lost to platform faults.

data.title: Neon now has realtime
data.summary: Neon's Realtime public beta turns SQL queries, including joins and aggregates, into live subscriptions that automatically update apps as Postgres data changes, without polling or a separate realtime service.

data.title: TabPFN
data.summary: TabPFN is a foundation model trained on synthetic datasets that performs classification and regression on new tabular data without training a separate model for each dataset.

design.title: Apple's App Store rules now explicitly ban AI nudify apps
design.summary: Apple has strengthened its App Store rules to explicitly address AI-generated nonconsensual intimate imagery and apps that digitally undress people. Developers must proactively moderate harmful user-generated content, while a clarified rule prohibits hiding functionality during review and enabling features such as nudification after approval. The changes follow months of criticism over harmful AI apps reaching the App Store and incidents involving tools such as Grok being used to create sexualized deepfakes.

design.title: Figma Opens Code Layers Beta, Adds Specs and a Backend for Make
design.summary: Figma Code Layers has entered open beta across plans, running interactive prototypes beside design frames, with generation and editing free on paid plans through November 4. Specs adds shared Markdown documents that pass requirements to AI agents through MCP, and a Payload integration gives Make a database, CMS, and admin interface. Rollouts differ: Guidelines is in open beta on paid plans, Code sources stays closed, and Payload reaches all plans over the coming weeks.

design.title: Apple calls iPhone Duo pre-order demand ‘extraordinary' as shipping dates slip
design.summary: Apple says iPhone Duo pre-order demand has been “nothing short of extraordinary,” with shipping estimates quickly slipping from October into January and even February in some countries. Limited initial supply appears to be amplifying the delays, while Apple says it is working to get devices to customers as quickly as possible and will continue accepting online orders. The shortages have already created a resale market, with scalpers listing pre-orders for prices as high as $10,000.

design.title: Use Feedback as Your Superpower: Learn, Improve, Shine
design.summary: Feedback is the lifeblood of great design, and how someone responds to it matters more than they might think. There are four types of feedback: positive, constructive, negative, and appreciation. Negative comments can be reframed by acknowledging emotions, separating self from work, and staying curious.

design.title: Design in the material you ship
design.summary: Digital designers should understand code as a material in the same way architects understand stone or steel, learning what it can do without necessarily mastering how to write it. AI increasingly handles implementation, making it practical to design and review working interfaces in code where responsive behavior, real data, loading states, accessibility, and failure conditions can be experienced rather than represented as static pictures. The valuable skill is therefore shifting from syntax toward understanding how software behaves, testing its limits, and judging whether the resulting product actually works for people.

design.title: Synthetic Users vs. Human Respondents: Same Conclusion, Less Variation
design.summary: A comparison of 120 synthetic respondents with 604 humans produced the same broad conclusion about terminology for UX work, but AI-generated responses showed dramatically less variation. Synthetic participants converged on roughly a dozen labels while humans produced more than 50, demonstrating a form of mode collapse that can erase unusual perspectives and differences between groups. Synthetic users may help generate hypotheses or identify broad patterns, but they cannot replace human research when unexpected responses, minority perspectives, or natural variation matter.

design.title: How Span Reimagined the Nature Museum Identity
design.summary: Span redesigned Chicago's Peggy Notebaert Nature Museum around the colors, forms, and character of native Illinois prairies, creating a warmer and more expressive identity for both casual visitors and scientific audiences. Tonka provides an organic wordmark, while New Atten, seven colors named after prairie flora, and an abstract mark that can read as a butterfly, flower, or cloud give the system its distinctive character. The mark can frame photography, become a repeating pattern, or function independently, allowing the identity to extend across the website, signage, campaigns, posters, and museum store.

design.title: Together gives Clusia a four-petal mark showing AI and people at work
design.summary: Together created Clusia's identity around a four-petal mark representing multiple people and AI systems working together inside the assurance platform, deliberately avoiding the robotic visual language common to AI companies. The petals become pixels in 3D illustrations, animate through product states, and combine with Die Grotesk, Vitruv Text, forest-inspired colors, and candid workplace photography to create a system that feels technological but distinctly human. Generative AI was used to explore illustration forms before they were rebuilt and refined in Cinema 4D, while the product itself uses a restrained version of the identity with green reserved for actions, statuses, and the animated mark.

Black Friday weekend offers the best selection and savings for electronics, shoes, fragrances, and appliances. Late December brings deeper discounts on cosmetics, handbags, and kitchenware. Search data also reveals last-minute shopping patterns. “Next day shipping” searches peak December 22, while “same day pickup” peaks December 24.

Viral Producers test entertaining campaigns that get people talking about a brand. Internet Comedians create culturally relevant content people want to share. Creator Deal Makers build partnerships that help creators grow their audiences while expanding brand reach. These roles help brands earn attention rather than compete on content volume alone.

marketing.title: Gated Content Is the #1 Enemy of AI Search
marketing.summary: Ungate content that helps buyers research categories and compare vendors to improve AI search visibility. Reserve forms for genuinely exclusive assets such as personalized ROI audits and proprietary data. For research reports, publish key findings and methodology on an accessible landing page while gating the full download. Noindex gated landing pages and hosted PDFs when appropriate to prevent them from competing with primary website content.

It recommends testing one workflow at a time and keeping human review before publication to catch errors and prevent broken automations from publishing inaccurate content.

marketing.title: How the AI boom might really end: 5 scenarios
marketing.summary: The AI boom may end not because demand disappears, but because profits shift away from major AI labs. Open-weight models are driving prices down while efficiency breakthroughs could reduce computing costs. AI companies risk failing to capture the value they create while chipmakers and infrastructure providers could still benefit from growing AI usage even if leading AI labs lose value.

marketing.title: What on earth is going on with AI pricing and packaging?
marketing.summary: AI companies are struggling to price products because usage costs vary widely and customers can't predict what credits or tokens will buy them. ChatGPT and Claude advertise vague usage limits, while Lovable sells credits without explaining what customers can build with them. Unlike traditional SaaS pricing based on seats or transactions, AI costs depend on the complexity of each task and the resources needed to complete it. Companies must make usage limits and costs easier to understand while managing unpredictable computing expenses and preventing abuse of free plans.

founders.title: Valuations Need a Correction
founders.summary: Startup valuation reports only include companies that managed to raise money. As fewer seed companies reach Series A, that group becomes increasingly selective. A model correcting for this bias estimates that new seed rounds value companies at four times the average existing seed startup. Higher round prices can therefore accompany a tougher fundraising market. Before using a recently funded competitor to price your own round, compare your growth and unit economics with theirs.

founders.title: Investors Turn on Data Center Builders as Rising Interest Rates Dampen the AI Trade
founders.summary: Rising interest rates and market skepticism challenge AI infrastructure firms like CoreWeave, which heavily rely on debt for growth. CoreWeave's bond trading reflects distress, and its founders selling $3.3 billion in stock since the IPO adds to investor unease. Meanwhile, AI token spending growth plateaus as new enterprise customer acquisition slows, amid efficiency improvements and cost reductions.

founders.title: What on earth is going on with AI pricing and packaging?
founders.summary: Lovable's growth lead says even her company's pricing is hard to understand. Its $25 monthly plan buys 100 credits, but customers have to start building to learn what those credits accomplish. General-purpose AI makes this harder because two requests for the same outcome can incur very different costs, especially when an agent retries its work. Credits help combine those costs into a subscription. The missing step is translating the allowance into work a buyer recognizes, as audio tools do with minutes and scraping tools do with pages.

founders.title: Negotiation & Multi-Turn Games
founders.summary: Negotiation works best as a collaborative process rather than a zero-sum contest. Understanding each side's priorities and constraints creates stronger, lasting outcomes across hiring, venture investments, sales, and acquisitions.

founders.title: App Store or web checkout: the math at 15%
founders.summary: Moving a small app's checkout to the web saves less than the headline App Store fee suggests. At Apple's 15% rate, a $9.99 subscription leaves $8.49 in the app versus about $9.33 after Stripe card and billing fees. With equal prices and renewals, losing roughly 9% of buyers erases that gain before extra operating costs. One small-business app in Adapty's review rolled back its test after revenue per paywall viewer fell 9%. Judge a checkout experiment on revenue per viewer through at least one renewal, using your actual fees.

founders.summary: G2's 2026 AI Agents Report reveals 91% of B2B buyers find per-seat pricing unfair, with 57% preferring usage-based models. Buyers expect stronger agent capabilities, with 74% open to switching vendors at renewal and 72% valuing a robust ecosystem. 46% find agent running costs higher than anticipated, demanding real-time dashboards and spend caps for better cost control.

SnapDocs began by helping offices manage mortgage signings, then gave notaries and attorneys their own profiles so they could work across customers on one platform. founders.title: How agents unlock new markets
founders.summary: Suppose a supplier turns down an order for 5,000 parts because it can only ship 2,000 immediately. The buyer can wait a month for the rest, but nobody asks. Agents representing both sides could work out a split delivery and save the order. Walmart already uses AI to negotiate individually with smaller suppliers. Those suppliers used to get standard terms because the savings were too small to justify negotiating each deal.

founders.title: Delta's Biscoff Cookies Were Supposed to Be Temporary. Then Passengers Fell in Love
founders.summary: A peanut shortage gave an unfamiliar Belgian cookie access to Delta's passengers in 1986. The airline says the replacement was supposed to be temporary, but passengers began calling headquarters to ask where they could buy Biscoff. Lotus answered with mail order in the 1990s, then entered major US grocery stores through Kroger in 2006. Delta now serves 70 million packs a year. For a product customers need to try first, look for a business that already serves them and needs something inexpensive to hand out, then give those customers somewhere to reorder.

crypto.title: Turkey confirms Hex founder Richard Heart's arrest
crypto.summary: Justice Minister Akın Gürlek confirmed Heart (Richard Schueler) was detained in Istanbul on October 14 with his wife, and three bodyguards were detained later. Searches of 15 addresses turned up $7.15M in cash, six cold wallets, seven firearms, 1,400 rounds, 28 watches, and 97 pieces of jewelry. Heart has been under an Interpol Red Notice since December 2024, issued for Finland over alleged gross tax evasion and assault. Gürlek also tied it to alleged $1B in crypto fraud. A US judge dismissed the SEC's case on jurisdictional grounds in February 2025, and the SEC did not refile.

crypto.summary: Circle reported about $1.4B in H1 2026 revenue. It paid $819M to USDC distribution partners and transaction costs and reinvested about $473M in infrastructure, compliance, and product. It kept about 7 cents of net profit per dollar of revenue. COO Kash Razzaghi's blog post pushes back on new stablecoin entrants who argue issuers keep too much. USDC processed over $36T onchain and had about 77% of global stablecoin transaction volume in June, up from 60% a year earlier. Q3 results are due November 4.

crypto.title: Lighter EVM Devnet Live with OpenVM and Axiom
crypto.summary: Lighter launched an EVM-equivalent rollup devnet, built with Axiom and proved by OpenVM, running alongside Lighter Core, their existing high-performance order book engine. Both execution layers settle to Ethereum with a single shared ZK proof, so the EVM rollup and the order book achieve joint finality in one proof cycle. Developers can deploy smart contracts on the EVM layer while Lighter Core handles order matching, with both environments settling atomically on Ethereum rather than through separate proof pipelines.

crypto.title: AI Is Making Ethereum More Ambitious: Formal Verification at Scale
crypto.summary: AI agents formally verified Ethereum's Fast Confirmation Rule (FCR) in Lean in 4-5 days, producing machine-checked safety proofs that FCR-confirmed blocks remain canonical under its assumptions. When researchers adapted the model to upcoming Gloas changes, the proof system surfaced a spec-level fork-choice bug before it shipped, pinpointing the exact failure cause. The Ethereum Foundation's earlier investments in formal verification infrastructure and post-quantum research now compound with AI tooling, with Lean already integrated into the BLS, KZG, SSZ, and consensus specs. The combination enables tighter fork timelines and more ambitious protocol features without reducing the security bar, with the upcoming Hegotá upgrade as the first test of this accelerated cadence.

crypto.title: GPUs Are Financed for Years. AI Workloads Run for Weeks
crypto.summary: GPU supply contracts lock capacity for 36 months while AI workloads demand compute for weeks. Hyperbolic exploits the duration mismatch by buying multi-year bare-metal capacity at contracted rates and reselling short-duration slots at a premium, growing from near-zero to $80M annualized revenue run-rate between June 2025 and September 2026. Neocloud lenders require contracted off-take, which structurally biases supply toward long-term commitments, and Hyperbolic hedges Year 3 tail risk with put options on compute prices to protect the back end. Exchange-traded GPU rental contracts are forming as compute follows the commodity arc from bilateral deals to traded benchmarks, with physical settlement as the foundation derivative indices build on, mirroring electricity's 30-year path from vertically integrated utilities to CME/ICE contracts.

crypto.title: The Wallet Wars
crypto.summary: AI agents require payment credentials to execute purchases, creating two distinct competitive fronts: who supplies the credential and who lets the agent transact with the user's full identity. Stripe's Link and Shopify's Shop Pay have moved fastest on integration, but Stripe's virtual-card approach routes purchases through a Stripe-issued card rather than the user's original card, stripping loyalty rewards and breaking direct merchant relationships. Visa, Mastercard, and AMEX are building scoped agentic tokens that map transactions back to the user's original card, preserving benefits that virtual-card intermediaries remove. The competitive trajectory mirrors the AOL-to-open-web shift: open-standard agentic tokens are positioned to displace proprietary virtual cards as the dominant payment layer for agents.

crypto.title: Network State Acquiring Farcaster

crypto.title: BIS: Stablecoins and bank deposits act as substitutes
crypto.summary: A BIS working paper using US data finds stablecoins and bank deposits are direct portfolio substitutes. A 1-basis-point rise in bank deposit rates cuts 10-week stablecoin market cap growth by about 3 percentage points, and by up to about 9 under an IV approach. The effect is stronger for USDC (-4.8%), which is tied to the US onshore market, than for offshore-focused USDT (-1.9%). It also holds against bank CD rates and DeFi lending yields. The conclusion is that bank deposit pricing acts as a drag on stablecoin growth.

fintech.title: Stripe says agentic commerce activity went “vertical” in September
fintech.summary: Stripe President John Collison says agent-driven commerce on Stripe began accelerating sharply in September, suggesting AI agents are starting to move from product discovery into actual purchasing. He argues that computer use was a key unlock because agents can now navigate existing websites and complete purchases without native integrations, while payments companies still need to solve issues such as authorization, liability, and merchant acceptance.

fintech.title: Winning the relay race: Long-running agents in high-value customer journeys
fintech.summary: The next major AI opportunity is “long-running agents” that own complex customer journeys across weeks or months, rather than completing isolated tasks. By maintaining context, coordinating sub-agents, and learning from each case, these systems could capture value that currently leaks across human handoffs and let vendors price against outcomes or revenue uplift, with go-to-market models ranging from software platforms to outsourced services to fully integrated AI-native businesses.

fintech.title: Visa Direct moves stablecoin-powered money movement from pilot to production
fintech.summary: Visa is moving stablecoin capabilities in Visa Direct into commercial production, with Inyo Global becoming the first partner to enable businesses to prefund cross-border payouts using USDC in near real time. The launch lets fintechs, money transmitters, and payment companies use stablecoins for 24/7 liquidity and funding while still relying on Visa Direct's existing global payout network, marking a shift from stablecoin experimentation toward day-to-day payments infrastructure.

fintech.title: Patrick Collison says Privy has scaled rapidly inside Stripe
fintech.summary: Patrick Collison says Privy has grown sharply since Stripe acquired it, with assets in wallets up about 25x, monthly active developers up 3x, revenue up 9x, and transaction volume approaching $25 billion per month. Stripe is now integrating Privy across Treasury, Link, and Connect while combining it with Bridge, fiat rails, cards, and stablecoins to build a programmable financial stack for both businesses and AI agents.

fintech.title: Mastercard and BVNK launch Global Money Platform for fiat and stablecoins
fintech.summary: Mastercard and BVNK launched Global Money Platform, a single API that combines multi-currency fiat and stablecoin accounts, real-time conversion, stablecoin-linked cards, and local bank payouts through Mastercard Move. The platform is designed to let banks, fintechs, and enterprises manage and embed global money movement from one infrastructure layer, with future support planned for agentic commerce and additional regulated forms of money such as tokenized deposits.

fintech.title: GI Partners CEO leaves after a year, delaying Fund VII plans
fintech.summary: GI Partners CEO and head of private equity Travis Pearson left the $49 billion firm after just over a year in the role, prompting GI to reconsider the timing of its seventh private equity fund and push the launch into 2027. The firm does not plan to name a new CEO, instead relying on its executive committee while three senior investors co-lead the private equity business.

fintech.title: AI-native payments platform Movere launches
fintech.summary: A collection of banking and fintech veterans has unveiled Movere, an AI-native payments platform for businesses.

fintech.title: Stripe and Plasma team on multi-currency stablecoin cards
fintech.summary: Stripe and Plasma today announced a collaboration to launch multi-currency stablecoin cards, making it easier for people and businesses to spend across currencies and markets.

fintech.title: The Next Phase of AI in Banking: From Pilots to Real Value
fintech.summary: Banks are asking an important question about artificial intelligence: where can it make a real difference in everyday operations?

it.title: Workday opens live enterprise data to AI agents
it.summary: Workday Data Cloud gives agents access to live business data, existing permissions, and business logic without requiring duplicate datasets or rebuilt security controls. Agent Lake and Live Data Query are generally available, while semantic models and tools for governed agent actions remain in early access.

it.title: Anthropic commits 5% of its shares to public benefit fund
it.summary: Anthropic is allocating 5% of its shares to a new fund that could support nonprofits and direct distributions to populations affected by AI. Together with founder and employee pledges, the company says roughly 20% of its equity is now dedicated to public benefit.

it.title: Microsoft plans to pay Anthropic over $2B a year to keep Copilot competitive
it.summary: Microsoft reportedly plans to pay Anthropic over $2 billion annually to use Claude AI models within its Copilot assistant. The integration responds to client performance pressures and aims to improve output on tasks like financial automation and presentations. To manage costs, Microsoft employs an internal model router that directs some workloads to OpenAI models.

it.title: If you can't automate your workflow, neither can your users' agents
it.summary: When developers struggle to automate their own workflows, AI coding agents will encounter the exact same friction, making workflow obstacles a critical product problem. Workflows designed around human navigation, portals, and undocumented knowledge cause high failure rates and excessive token costs for agents. Developers should evaluate their products by testing them with goal-oriented agent prompts rather than relying solely on usage telemetry or manual workarounds.

it.title: ServiceNow AI Control Tower: Selling a penthouse while building the frame
it.summary: ServiceNow's AI Control Tower provides a strong governance workflow and system of action for enterprise AI. However, customer interviews reveal that claims of end-to-end technical governance and a universal runtime kill switch are overstated, with runtime enforcement typically handled by external or custom tools. Additionally, customers face meaningful friction regarding configuration costs, CMDB hygiene, and pricing tier uplifts.

it.title: What happens when AI agents work more hours than employees?
it.summary: Anthropic's internal research found that interactive agent hours outnumbered employee hours six to one by August, while output increased and junior technical roles represented a smaller share of hiring. Human attention is becoming a bottleneck, pushing employees toward monitoring agent pipelines and hiring managers toward prioritizing judgment and autonomy.

it.title: ServiceNow Plans AI Passport for Enterprise Agents
it.summary: ServiceNow's AI Passport is a governance tool designed to control and verify the permissions of artificial-intelligence agents during execution. Nvidia is a design and launch partner for the tool, which is expected to become available in the fourth quarter of 2026 alongside other enterprise products.

it.title: Honeywell launches AI agents to manage building alarms, maintenance and energy
it.summary: Honeywell Technologies has introduced Forge Cognition, a platform combining AI agents with live facility simulations to help operators manage building alarms, maintenance, and energy use. Developed using technology from NVIDIA and Dell Technologies, the platform offers adjustable automation ranging from manual to autonomous oversight. Early pilot testing at NVIDIA's Voyager campus and other sites demonstrated significant reductions in unnecessary alerts and potential energy savings.

it.title: AI pricing tools face a consumer trust problem
it.summary: Retailers are adopting AI-assisted pricing and digital shelf labels, but consumers remain confused about how personal data influences prices. The reporting separates actual practices from misconceptions and highlights how limited transparency can undermine trust in otherwise routine technology upgrades.

it.title: Firefox Enterprise 158 puts browser policy, data controls and AI governance on customer-run infrastructure
it.summary: Mozilla announced the early access of Firefox Enterprise 158, featuring a self-hosted admin console, domain-scoped data-loss prevention, and governance controls for AI tools. Aimed at organizations in France, Germany, Austria, and Switzerland, the management plane runs on customer infrastructure rather than relying solely on cloud-hosted alternatives or standard MDM policies.

it.title: AI and SaaS workloads drive Akamai cloud adoption
it.summary: Akamai reports new cloud deployments spanning GPU workloads, disaster recovery, and a developer platform migrating nearly 1,500 microservices from a major hyperscaler to reduce costs.

it.title: The AI NOC Engineer: Building an Autonomous DevOps Agent with Amazon Q and CloudWatch
it.summary: The architecture uses Amazon SQS, AWS Fargate, and LangGraph for cyclical agentic reasoning, Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Q for root cause analysis, and AWS Step Functions to implement a Human-in-the-Loop Slack approval gate before executing automated remediation.

hardware.title: Intel and Qualcomm reportedly bid up to $10B for Tenstorrent on an unverified cost claim
hardware.summary: Intel and Qualcomm are reportedly bidding up to $10 billion for Tenstorrent, whose roughly $1,000 Blackhole chips run the BlockFloat8 number format natively, where GPUs with native support list near $40,000. Smallest.ai says its text-to-speech model, with over 80% running in 8-bit, costs about a quarter as much to run as on Nvidia's L40S. The figures are vendor-published and unverified, and no deal has closed.

hardware.title: CXMT swings to a nearly $20B nine-month profit as AI demand drives up DRAM prices
hardware.summary: CXMT expects nine-month net profit of 131 to 132.5 billion yuan ($19.6 to $19.8 billion), versus a 5.3 billion yuan loss a year earlier, on revenue of 265 to 270 billion yuan, up from 32.1 billion. It credits AI-driven DRAM shortages, expanded capacity, and more output per wafer. Its claim of fifth-generation DRAM in mass production hasn't been independently verified, and memory booms typically fund new capacity that eventually pulls prices back down.

hardware.title: NASA's Roman telescope beats its image-quality spec by nearly 30% after a hair-width mirror nudge
hardware.summary: After moving Roman's secondary mirror by about one-sixteenth the width of a human hair, engineers measured 63 nanometers RMS of optical error in the Wide Field Instrument, nearly 30% better than the 90-nanometer requirement. The camera has 18 detectors, and the same adjustment fixed slight defocus in the Coronagraph Instrument, which still needs testing of its ability to block unwanted light. Roman launched August 30, and both instruments now match or beat predictions.

hardware.title: Tesla Roadster pairs underbody suction fans with cold-gas thrusters for grip beyond what tires allow
hardware.summary: The Roadster's floor uses fans and perimeter seals to pull air out from under the car, creating up to 2 g of suction, enough to hold it upside down while stationary, and at speed, front and rear passages open for more flow. Cold-gas thrusters add a second system: ten nozzles fed by compressed air, with all-electric actuators for fast micro-adjustments, which Tesla says push with four to five times the force tires can deliver.

hardware.title: Variable frequency drives could free up grid power by cutting motor energy use 40 to 60 percent
hardware.summary: Variable frequency drives adjust motor speed to match demand, cutting a motor's energy use by about 40 to 60 percent. Toyota saved over $700,000 a year after putting them on 200-plus HVAC motors at its Kentucky plant, in a $1.25 million pilot. Cheaper sensors, machine-learning control, and power chips borrowed from EVs and solar inverters have cut costs. ABB claims drives on every motor could cover up to five years of data center load growth.

hardware.title: Spin waves coupled to a superconducting circuit create a one-way street for microwave signals
hardware.summary: Argonne and UIUC researchers coupled spin waves in a thin yttrium iron garnet film to a superconducting resonator built directly on top, creating a hybrid mode that propagates one way and could keep return noise from leaking back into qubits. The key materials fix was swapping the usual rare-earth-containing substrate, which absorbs microwaves at low temperatures, for one without rare-earth metals. It's still a proof of concept.

hardware.title: Kornia-SLAM: Visual-Inertial Odometry and SLAM in Rust
hardware.summary: Kornia-SLAM is an open-source visual-inertial odometry and spatial mapping library implemented entirely in Rust. It supports monocular, stereo, and RGB-D cameras coupled with inertial measurement units, utilizing factor graph optimization to maintain real-time performance and strict memory safety. This framework gives embedded software teams a reliable, crash-resilient foundation for real-time spatial estimation on compute-limited physical devices.

hardware.title: Gemini 4 Argon: Multimodal Foundation Models for Embodied Intelligence
hardware.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 4 Argon, a multimodal foundation model engineered specifically for embodied physical systems. Featuring native spatio-temporal reasoning and low-latency action generation, it links high-level semantic understanding directly to robot execution through native bridges for ROS 2 and physics simulators like MuJoCo. The architecture allows creators of intelligent physical machines to translate natural language goals into dexterous, real-world manipulation and navigation.

hardware.title: AMD shows how to hand-tune an FP16 GEMM kernel on RDNA 3 and RDNA 4 to match hipBLASLt
hardware.summary: AMD walks through eight steps to build an FP16 GEMM kernel on RDNA 3 and RDNA 4, taking the RX 9070 XT from 150 ms to 8.71 ms on an 8192-cubed multiply, versus 8.05 ms for hipBLASLt.

hardware.title: Terminal RViz: Terminal-Based 3D Visualizer for ROS 2
hardware.summary: Terminal RViz renders 3D ROS 2 sensor data, point clouds, and robot states directly inside a terminal window using Braille Unicode characters and a software-based renderer.

hardware.title: ASPIRE: Agentic Skill Discovery and Policy Synthesis
hardware.summary: ASPIRE is an autonomous framework from NVIDIA Research that enables robots to discover, practice, and catalog manipulation skills in simulation without human supervision.

hardware.title: Apple and Meta tune an 816B-parameter open model to run on two M5 Ultra Mac Studios
hardware.summary: Meta's 816-billion-parameter Muse Spark Open model, a mixture-of-experts design with 42 billion active per token, is tuned to run locally on clustered M5 Ultra Mac Studios using Apple's MLX framework.

hardware.title: HUMXN pays for home repairs in three cities to record wearable-sensor data for robot training
hardware.summary: HUMXN, a Minneapolis AI data company, will pay for qualifying plumbing, electrical, HVAC, air-duct, and carpet-cleaning jobs in Minneapolis, Chicago, and Miami in exchange for letting technicians work in homes wearing capture gear that records their jobs.
